{"title":"Fix invoice totals off by a cent","brief":"Owner report: some invoice totals are off by one cent. Fix it so totals are exact.

Likely cause (verify first): src/invoices/index.ts `lineTotalCents` does `Math.floor(line.unitPrice * 100) * line.quantity`. Floating-point makes e.g. 0.29 * 100 = 28.999..., which floors to 28, so the line loses a cent per unit. Reproduce first: add failing unit tests in src/invoices/index.test.ts with prices like 0.29, 0.57, 1.15, 4.35, 19.99, 0.07 and several quantities, plus a multi-line invoice, and confirm the wrong totals before fixing. Also check the Invoices page (src/web/server.ts, tests/browser/invoices.spec.ts) shows the corrected total.

Fix: convert unit prices to integer cents with correct rounding (e.g. Math.round(unitPrice * 100)), then multiply by quantity and sum in integer cents. Do not leave any float-to-cent truncation anywhere in the invoice path. Keep the code style of the file (small exported arrow functions).

Done when: new tests fail before the fix and pass after; `npm test`, `npm run lint` and the browser spec pass; CHANGELOG.md has an entry (CI checks for it via scripts/check-changelog.mjs). Dates in the UI are always DD/MM/YYYY - do not change invoiceDate behaviour. Never run scripts/owner-only.sh. Work in your worktree and open a pull request. Context: src/web/server.ts serves /customers as an HTML table (Name, VAT) from the store in src/customers/index.ts (Customer = id, name, vat, createdAt ISO string). There is also /api/customers returning JSON.

Build:
- A CSV endpoint (e.g. GET /customers.csv or /api/customers.csv) returning all customers with `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8` and `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="customers.csv"`. Note the current routing uses `request.url?.startsWith('/customers')` for the HTML page, so make sure the CSV route is matched before it or routing is made exact.
- Columns: Name, VAT, Created. Created must be formatted DD/MM/YYYY (owner rule: dates in the UI are always DD/MM/YYYY).
- Proper RFC 4180 escaping: quote fields containing commas, quotes, CR/LF; double embedded quotes. Guard against CSV/formula injection (prefix cells starting with =, +, -, @, tab or CR with a single quote). Use CRLF line endings; a header row always, even with zero customers.
- Put the CSV building in a small pure function (e.g. in src/customers) with unit tests.
- A visible "Export CSV" link/button on the Customers page that downloads the file. Text label, no emoji. Make it look clean next to the heading/table.
- Extend tests/browser/customers.spec.ts to click the export and check the downloaded content.

Done when: `npm test`, `npm run lint`, and the browser specs pass; CHANGELOG.md has an entry (CI checks it via scripts/check-changelog.mjs). Never run scripts/owner-only.sh.
